text: There is a small town where many different animals live.
A rooster named Chicken Little is one of the animals, and he spends his days on a farm.
Everyday he eats seeds and plays under a tall oak tree.
One sunny morning, Chicken Little lies down under the oak tree when he hears a rustling sound in the leaves above him
He looks up to check for what was making the noise, when an acorn comes falling down from the branches and hits him on the head.
Chicken Little does not see what hit him, and thinks the sky is falling.
His heart pounds, and he says out loud,
"Oh no! If the sky is falling, I need to warn everyone before the stars and moon fall too!"
He runs off down the path towards the rest of the town.

text: Chicken Little spreads panic.

text: When you have a problem, slowing down helps us make calm and thoughtful decisions.
Chicken Little notices the acorn on the ground and sees more acorns in the tree above.
He has never seen an acorn fall like that, but now he knows what hit him.
Chicken Little stares at the acorn for a while.
"Hmm…the sky did not fall on me just now, but what if it falls next?" he wonders.
He decides to find his friends and ask for their help to answer his question, just to be safe.
He walks to the pond and finds his friend Duckie swimming.
"Duckie! I am scared something bad might be happening, and I would like your help," Chicken Little tells her.
Duckie replies, "I am sorry to hear you are feeling scared! What happened and how can I help you?"
Chicken Little is happy Duckie is so caring, but he is still quite upset about the acorn.

text: Carefully thinking about what to do in big groups can be a great idea to make sure everyone gets to share what they are thinking.
Once they hear all the ideas, their friend the bear suggests the group go to the wise old farmer who lives nearby to ask what he thinks.
Everyone thinks this is a great idea, and so they walk down to the farmer's house.
Outside the farmer's house, the wise man listens carefully and then shows everyone one of the trees on his farm.
It is the same kind of tree that Chicken Little was lying under.
The farmer shakes the tree gently, and a bunch of acorns fall out.
"Sometimes they fall, but that is not a bad thing! It is how the tree plants its seeds," the farmer says.
"Oh!" Chicken Little says, laughing with relief. "It was just an acorn after all!"
The friends smile at each other.
They felt proud that they worked together, stayed calm, and made thoughtful choices throughout the day.
